name: Telugu AI Calling — Vobiz + LiveKit + Groq + Cartesia

parameters.content:
## 📞 Telugu AI Calling — n8n orchestrator
**Vobiz (SIP) ⇄ LiveKit ⇄ Groq (STT + LLM) ⇄ Cartesia Sonic-3 (Telugu TTS)**

n8n *places and tracks* calls. The live voice conversation runs in the LiveKit agent worker (`agent.py`) — n8n cannot stream audio.

### Setup (5 min)
1. Edit the `CONFIG` block at the top of the 3 Code nodes: **Prepare Call**, **Prepare Report**, **Prepare Clone**
2. Self-hosted n8n: set env `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto` (needed to sign the LiveKit JWT)
3. Run `agent.py` with the same `AGENT_NAME` and your n8n *call-ended* URL
4. Activate this workflow, then use the production URLs

### Endpoints (all need header `x-webhook-secret`)
- `POST /webhook/telugu-call-start` → place a call
- `POST /webhook/telugu-call-ended` → agent posts transcript here
- `POST /webhook/telugu-voice-clone` → clone a voice (multipart)

### A · Place a call
body: `{ "phone": "9876543210", "name": "Ravi", "purpose": "...", "first_message": "(optional Telugu opener)", "voice_id": "(optional Cartesia id)", "variables": {} }`

### B · Call finished → Groq analysis → your backend
Agent posts the transcript here when the call ends. Groq returns summary / outcome / follow-up, then it is forwarded to `RESULT_WEBHOOK_URL` (optional).

### C · Clone a voice with Cartesia
multipart: file field `clip` (mp3/wav/ogg/webm, ~10–30 s clean speech) + `name` (+ optional `language`, `description`). Returns `voice_id` to use in Flow A / `CARTESIA_VOICE_ID`.
